sights.n: Kakazu Ridge — Kakazu Takadai Park (嘉数高台公園)
sights.w: One of the fiercest battlefields of the 1945 Battle of Okinawa: US forces attacked Kakazu Ridge on 9 April 1945 and needed about 15 days to take it, with thousands dead on both sides. Today a hilltop park with a globe-shaped observation deck looking over Futenma Air Station and toward the Maeda Escarpment, plus surviving pillboxes.

sights.n: Haebaru Army Hospital Shelter No. 20 (南風原陸軍病院壕 20号壕)
sights.w: Hand-dug tunnel used as a ward of the Okinawa Army Hospital in 1945, where the Himeyuri student nurses were first assigned before the retreat south. Guided visits by appointment through the Haebaru Town Culture Center (¥300).

sights.n: Minatogawa Stateside Town (港川ステイツサイドタウン)
sights.w: A neighbourhood of 1950s–60s white single-storey 'foreign houses' built for US military families, now converted into cafés, bakeries, galleries and shops. Lanes are named after US states (Oregon, Arizona, Michigan, Kansas and more); about 5 minutes' walk from the Minatogawa bus stop.
